Subject: Capacity sizing proposal for Dedicated renewal — Atlas Retail

Joe — following up on our renewal conversation. We’re preparing the dedicated capacity proposal for your June renewal and want to validate the traffic assumptions before we lock in reserved pools and the pricing tier.

Quick asks:
- Can you confirm expected 99th percentile QPS and peak QPS over the next 12 months (monthly bucketed is fine).
- Typical tokens per request for your customer-facing chat (and for nightly batch embeddings).
- Any hard latency SLOs (p50/p90/p99) we should size for.

We're planning a staged expansion option: an initial reserved pool to cover baseline traffic with autoscale burst for seasonal peaks, and an optional fast lane (low-latency pool) for your chat service. Initial internal estimate is +6 H100-class GPUs for low-latency and +4 A10G-class for embeddings to cover a 3x QPS growth baseline — but that will change with your numbers. Attached: traffic template to fill (atlas_traffic_forecast.xlsx).

I’ll loop in Rishi and Stephanie for pricing and commercial options once we have your numbers.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Growth, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Marissa — thanks, attached is our filled forecast (see atlas_traffic_forecast.xlsx). Summary below:
- Current baseline (Feb 2026): avg QPS = 120, peak QPS = 480 (seasonal spikes).
- Forecasted avg QPS by end of Q2 (June): 260; by end of Q3: 420; by end of Q4: 610.
- Typical chat tokens per request: 550 tokens (median), 1,200 tokens (peak flows).
- Nightly batch embedding jobs: ~1.1B tokens/day, executed between 02:00–05:00 local.
- Latency SLOs: p50 <= 90ms, p90 <= 220ms, p99 <= 450ms for the chat fast lane. Embedding jobs are throughput-first, latency not strict.

We want a guaranteed baseline to avoid throttling during promo windows; can tolerate short burst errors during extreme peaks if notified.

Joe Bennett
VP Product, Atlas Retail
joe.bennett@atlasretail.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-02-05T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity sizing proposal for Dedicated renewal — Atlas Retail

All — analyzed Joe's forecast and modeled options. Key assumptions: median request = 550 tokens, inference model = r-instruct-13B-quant (approx performance profile), average tokens generated per response = 250, target concurrency headroom = 1.5x for safety, and embedding batch windows are scheduled off-peak.

Sizing summary (recommended):
- Option A (conservative, latency-first): 8x H100-equivalent GPUs in a low-latency reserved pool (covers p99 target with 15% headroom for June->Q3 growth). Add 2x A10G-equivalent GPUs in a separate reserved pool for embedding jobs.
- Option B (cost-balanced, staged): 6x H100 low-latency + 4x A10G embedding, with autoscale burst of up to +4 H100-equivalents for predictable promo spikes (30 min cold start to elastic capacity). This supports ~420 QPS steady by Q3 and allows growth to ~600 QPS with managed bursts.
- Option C (aggressive, growth-proof): 12x H100 + 6x A10G reserved — guarantees 99th latency under 450ms for up to 700 QPS steady. Higher commit and lower unit price.

Rationale and rough throughput math: an H100-equivalent slot (our optimized runtime) sustains ~80 S2-like requests/sec at 550 tokens/req with p90 latency ~180ms when serving the r-instruct-13B-quant profile under continuous batching. With 6 H100 that's ~480 rps (requests per second) peak sustainable; factoring 1.5x headroom => ~320 sustained QPS. To hit 420 sustained QPS you need ~8 H100 equivalents. Embeddings are much cheaper per GPU; 4 A10G equivalents handle current embedding batch window comfortably; add 2 for lower nightly runtime.

Operational notes:
- We recommend separate reserved pools (fast-lane vs batch) so embedding jobs never interfere with chat SLOs.
- Plan for a canary: stage +4 GPUs into low-latency pool for 48 hours, validate p99 and error rates, then commit remaining GPUs.
- Provisioning lead time: ~3 weeks for Dedicated reservations to spin up in our DC and 1 week for configuration + canary.

I’ll attach a short provisioning runbook after Marissa confirms option.

—Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.ai

Joe / Marissa — pricing options attached (redwood_quote_v2.pdf). Short summary:
- Option A: higher per-unit price, month-to-month reserved pool (recommended for first renewal) — gives flexibility, 2-week cancellation with prorated credit.
- Option B: 12-month committed discount (15% off unit price) with ability to request 2 scheduled capacity changes per year.
- Option C: 24-month deep-commit (25% off) + lower provisioning lead time guarantee (SLA-backed).

Commercial considerations: we can tier the billing to separate fast-lane vs batch metering so Atlas only pays committed rate for reserved baseline and bursts billed at on-demand for elastic capacity. I included estimated monthly spend for each option in the PDF.

Next steps: pick sizing option (A/B/C) and commercial term. We can finalize SOW and route DocuSign once sizing and terms lock.

—Rishi
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai
